hero.subheadline: Worldwide open call for original digital art, free to enter
hero.valueProposition: Four awards, an exhibition in a physical gallery and a metaverse gallery, and a certificate for every participant in a free, AI-free digital art contest.

content.whyJoin:
The International Digital Art Contest 2026 is organized by the Academy of Fine Arts at the University of Mostar in Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is a free open call that asks artists to submit one original digital artwork created without AI tools, in either a still image or moving image category. Because there is no predefined theme, the contest is an unusual chance to present the work that best reflects your personal artistic practice rather than fitting a brief.

Selected works are shown in two simultaneous exhibitions: in the physical gallery of the Academy of Fine Arts in Siroki Brijeg and in the Academy's virtual gallery on the Spatial metaverse platform. Every participant receives a certificate of participation, and a digital catalog of selected works is published after the exhibition opens. Four awards are granted overall, including a Grand Prix and two first prizes in the still and moving image categories.

No entry fee is required, and both older and newly created works are accepted. The contest is open to artists from around the world aged 18 and above, with individual submissions only.
content.whoShouldApply:
This call is for digital artists aged 18 and above who create still images such as digital painting, digital graphics, or digital photography, or moving-image works such as short films and animations. It suits individual artists working without AI tools who want their work seen in both a physical gallery and a virtual metaverse exhibition.

It is not suited to teams, since collaborative works are not considered, nor to artists whose work is purely physical, because only works that exist exclusively in a digital environment with no physical equivalent are eligible. Applied or commercial works such as illustrations, posters, and design solutions created for clients are not accepted.
benefits: Exhibition of selected work in the physical gallery of the Academy of Fine Arts in Siroki Brijeg and in the Academy's virtual gallery on the Spatial metaverse platform
Certificate of participation for every applicant
A digital catalog of selected works published after the exhibition opening and available through the Academy's online channels
Awards across four prizes: Grand Prix, First Prize for Digital Still Image Artworks, First Prize for Digital Moving Image Artworks, and Special Jury Award
tips: Submit through the Google Forms link on the official contest page, not by email, and include a link to your artwork stored on a cloud service
Ensure the artwork link allows viewing without login and stays active until the end of the selection process
Name your artwork file using the format FirstName_LastName_Country_Code
For still images use JPG in RGB color space up to 20 MB; for moving images use MP4 with H.264 codec, up to 2 minutes and 500 MB
If you are asked to, be ready to provide working file versions, sketches, or other documentation proving the work was created without AI tools
Only submit works with no physical equivalent that were not created for commercial purposes or previous competitions

faq.question: Is there an entry fee?
faq.answer: No. Participation in the International Digital Art Contest 2026 is free of charge.

faq.question: Who can apply and how many works can an artist submit?
faq.answer: Artists from around the world who are at least 18 years old at the time of submission are eligible. Each applicant may submit one artwork only, and submissions must be individual; collaborative works are not considered.

faq.question: What formats are accepted?
faq.answer: Two categories are accepted: Digital Still Image Artworks (JPG, RGB color space, up to 20 MB) and Digital Moving Image Artworks (MP4 with H.264 codec, up to 2 minutes and 500 MB). Only works that exist exclusively in a digital environment with no physical equivalent are eligible.

faq.question: Are AI-generated works accepted?
faq.answer: No. Only digital artworks created without the use of artificial intelligence tools may be submitted. If the organizer suspects AI use, they may request documentation of the work process such as working file versions, sketches, or original project files.

faq.question: When will results be announced and where are the exhibitions held?
faq.answer: Results are announced on September 15, 2026. Selected works are shown in the physical gallery of the Academy of Fine Arts in Siroki Brijeg and in the Academy's virtual gallery on the Spatial platform, both opening October 14, 2026 and running until November 18, 2026.

faq.question: Is there a theme that must be followed?
faq.answer: No. The contest has no predetermined theme. Artists are free to submit a work that best reflects their artistic approach, research, or personal digital identity.

submissionGuide.detail: Create one original digital artwork without AI tools. For still images use JPG in RGB color space up to 20 MB; for moving images use MP4 with H.264 codec, up to 2 minutes and 500 MB. Name the file FirstName_LastName_Country_Code.

Upload the artwork to a cloud service such as Google Drive, WeTransfer, or Dropbox. Ensure the link allows viewing without login, for example by setting it to Anyone with the link can view, and keep it active until selection ends.
Submit exclusively through the Google Forms link on the official contest page at alu.sum.ba. Submissions sent by email are not considered.
Results are announced on September 15, 2026 on the official website of the Academy of Fine Arts Siroki Brijeg. Only authors whose works are selected for exhibition are notified by email.

Selected works are exhibited from October 14 to November 18, 2026, with simultaneous openings at 7:00 PM local time in the physical gallery in Siroki Brijeg and the virtual gallery on the Spatial platform.
